questions.q: In the new design, how does Bronze ingestion decide which source files to read?
options: It reads the watermark in meta.last_ingested_date and only reads files newer than it
It reads every source file that has ever existed, every single run
It randomly samples a subset of source files each night
It reads files in alphabetical order until it hits a time limit
questions.explain: The watermark table records the latest date already ingested, so each run only reads source files or partitions dated after it.

questions.q: What replaces "rebuild the whole table" for silver.sales_clean in the new design?
options: A MERGE INTO that inserts new rows and updates matching rows, keyed on transaction_id
Dropping and recreating the table from scratch every run, same as before
Deleting all existing rows and only keeping the newest day
A full table scan with no key, matching on every column at once
questions.explain: MERGE INTO matches incoming Bronze rows against silver.sales_clean on transaction_id, the table's true unique key, inserting new rows and updating existing ones.

questions.q: Why does Gold change the least of the three layers in this redesign?
options: Because it still just aggregates from Silver, and Silver is now small and current, not full history
Because Gold tables are never rebuilt in any pipeline design
Because the Regional Manager asked for no changes to Gold at all
Because Delta Lake doesn't allow MERGE INTO on Gold tables
questions.explain: Gold keeps aggregating from Silver the same way it always did; what changed is that Silver itself is now a small, current slice instead of the whole history, so Gold's cost per run stays low without Gold itself needing new incremental logic.

questions.q: What is a watermark, in the plain-English definition this lesson gives?
options: A saved checkpoint value marking what's already been processed, so the next run knows what's new
A digital signature embedded in each source file to prevent tampering
A visual overlay added to Power BI reports for branding purposes
The maximum file size Bronze is allowed to ingest in one run
questions.explain: The lesson defines a watermark as a saved checkpoint — here, a date — marking everything already processed, so the next run can tell what's new.

questions.q: In the five-step end-to-end plan, what happens immediately after ingesting new Bronze rows?
options: MERGE INTO silver.sales_clean on transaction_id, using only the newly-ingested rows
Advance the watermark before anything else happens
Rebuild gold.daily_sales_summary directly from the raw source files
Delete the watermark table and start over
questions.explain: The plan reads: ingest new Bronze rows, then MERGE INTO Silver using just those rows, then rebuild both Gold tables, then advance the watermark last.
